script: In 1961, the CIA spent twenty million dollars turning a live cat into a spy, and the mission lasted four minutes. The file was called Acoustic Kitty, and it was exactly as stupid as it sounds. Surgeons put a microphone in the cat's ear, a transmitter at the base of its skull, and an antenna down its tail, which the report calls a minor modification. The plan was to walk this animal past Soviet diplomats in a Washington park and record every word. Trainers spent five years teaching a cat to walk in a straight line toward a target. Nobody in that building ever asked the one question a child could have answered. On the first mission, agents opened the van door, and the cat walked straight into a passing taxi. That is case two forty one in an archive that never runs out, and there is a new one here tomorrow. The internal review called the project a success in principle, which is the most government sentence ever written. Then they classified the whole thing for thirty six years. Send this to whoever still believes your tax money is being watched carefully. Twenty million dollars, five years, one cat: mistake, or just a Tuesday?

description:
1961: Project Acoustic Kitty. The CIA surgically implanted a microphone, a transmitter and an antenna into a live cat, trained it for five years, and sent it to eavesdrop on Soviet diplomats in Washington. On its first mission it walked into a taxi. The internal review called it a success 'in principle'. Declassified in 2001.
